How to care for your animals

Open the menu and select the animal tab, you can check the current status of your animals in all of your pastures and barns. All necessary information like their age, health and productivity as well as the amount of food and water are displayed here. Please note, barns don’t need extra water.
Bring the correct food for the animal to the pasture/barn and load it into the food area. You can use the animal food pallets or Big bags - which will be more expensive in the long term - or feed them products from your harvests.
You can see if you have fed them correctly by looking at the health bar. It increases over time, and if it does, the animals will start to produce and are able to reproduce when they are old enough.

You can either sell the animals themselves, if you focus on breeding them, or sell their products. Products can be sold directly to selling stations. If you own factories, you can bring them there and continue processing. This will earn you more money, when selling the end product.

In Farming Simulator, there are cows that produce milk and cows that don't. Different breeds of cows provide a different amount of milk and also achieve a different selling price. Brown-Swiss and Holstein cows are used for dairy farming, while Angus and Limousin are only bred to be sold for profit. Total Mixed Ration (TMR) is the best food for cows and will maximize their milk production - find more information about this type of feeding in the respective section on how to produce Total Mixed Ration.

Get a dog house in the build mode menu and let a four-legged friend move in with you. You can only have one dog per farm. You can feed it, pet it and let it play with the ball. Take the dog on long walks into nature as it will follow you as long as you want.
The dog does not appear in the animal menu.

You can buy the animals directly at the pasture/barn and they will be delivered for a small fee. Alternatively, if you have bought a trailer, you can drive it to the animal dealership and buy them on-site to transport them yourself.
If you want to take a break from harvesting, or if that is not your main activity, you can also take care of animals: horses, cows, sheep, pigs, and chickens.

The first thing you need for your animals are pastures and barns. Depending on your money and plans, you can choose between small pastures and different sizes of barns. The larger the housing for the animal, the more you can own.
Open the construction menu and navigate to the animals tab. Place the pasture or barn on your farm.
While stables have a water connection, pastures must be supplied with water. For this you need a tractor and a trailed water tank.

Manure is not produced automatically. First, you have to add a separate manure heap next to your cow or pig barn. You can find it in the build mode menu.
Then, you have to bring straw as bedding to the dedicated area of the barn. Both loose straw and straw bales will be accepted as bedding.

Whether animals reproduce depends on three factors: Their age, the space available and the health of the animals. When they reach the age of maturity, they can give birth to offspring. But this is only possible if there is room for more animals in the barn, of course. Also, their health has to be at 100%. You can achieve this by feeding the animals with proper food.

Food: Grass and hay Product: Goat milk Age of maturity: 8 months
Farming Simulator 25 marks the first appearance of Goats in the game series. These animals require the same facilities as sheep for grazing and thriving.
They produce a unique type of milk, Goat Milk, that needs to be retrieved from the barns in form of milk tank pallets. This milk can be processed into Goat cheese from a Dairy production point.

Food: Hay, oat and sorghum Age of maturity: 22 months
Horses are trained and then sold for a profit. You can choose between multiple breeds: gray, pinto, palomino, chestnut, bay, black, seal brown and dun. The difference is purely visual.
When you buy a horse it is given a name automatically. You can change its name in the animal menu. Each horse also has an individual fitness level. The higher the fitness level, the higher the value. Raise their fitness level by riding them.
It is also important to take care of the horses' hygiene. If you look at a horse with the cursor, you will see an information box in the lower right corner. You should brush your mounts regularly to maintain their health. When you look at the horse, the symbol of a brush appears, and you then press the respective button to interact.
Make sure that you ride your horses regularly. When you are sitting on the horse, you will see your riding progress in the top left corner when the controls help window is active. Ride each horse 100% every day. This is the only way to increase their physical condition and thus their value when you sell them.

Food: Corn, wheat, barley, canola, sunflowers, soybeans, potatoes, sorghum and sugar beets Product: Manure and slurry Age of maturity: 6 months
In Farming Simulator, there are different breeds of pigs: German Landrace, Bentheim Black Pied, and Berkshire. There's no real difference, except for their visual appearance.
When it comes to providing food for pigs, they are the most time-consuming animal, because you need to feed them a variety of crops you need to grow yourself. As an alternative, you can buy pig food - which is of course more expensive in the long run.
To maintain the health of your pigs, and therefore their ability to reproduce, you need to provide them with the right mix of feed. You just unload the pig food or each crop at the unloading area of the pigsty. You don't need to use a mixing wagon - which is required for cows.
Base: either corn or sorghum Grains: either wheat or barley Protein: either soybeans, canola, or sunflowers Root crops: either potatoes or sugar beet

Food: Grass and hay Product: Wool Age of maturity: 8 months
In Farming Simulator, there are four breeds of sheep: Landrace of Bentheim, Steinschaf, Swiss Black-Brown Mountain, and Black Welsh Mountain. The only difference is their appearance.
In order to sell the wool, you have to grab the pallet at the sheep pasture with a pallet fork and transport it to the spinnery or bring it to your own production point for further processing.
You can optimize the milk production of your cows by feeding them Total Mixed Ration (TMR). This is the only way to gain 100% productivity.

Straw, hay, silage and mineral feed. You can harvest grass, and turn it into hay yourself, if your farm has fields of grass and the required machines.
It's easier to buy all the ingredients at the dealership. You can buy bales of straw, hay and silage under "objects" > "bales". Mineral feed is available in the "pallets" section.

Then, you have to prepare the feed in a forage mixer and deliver it to the barn. In the forage mixer you have to add straw, hay, silage and mineral feed in the right ratio. The mixer will show you the correct mixing ratio when being near the mixer wagon.
Do you use a mixer wagon instead of a robot?

Then, you only need to deliver the ingredients to the barn (straw, hay, silage and mineral feed). The robot will automatically mix the feed and feed the animals regularly if all ingredients are in stock.
Do you have a barn with a feeding robot?

Food: Grass, hay, and TMR Product: Milk, manure, and slurry Age of maturity: 18 months
Farming Simulator 25 marks the first appearance of Water Buffaloes in the game series. These animals require the same facilities as cows for grazing and thriving.
They produce a unique type of milk, Buffalo Milk, that can be processed into delicious Buffalo Mozzarella in a Dairy production point.

Shipping containers come in different sizes and they can be used to transport logs. You can purchase them in the shop, but need to load them onto a lowloader like the Schwarzmüller 3A or similar vehicle. To load the container onto the lowloader a fitting pallet fork and the proper wheel loader are required. The container has an autoload function so filling it up with trees is easy. Make sure to load trees that have the same length as your shipping container, otherwise you will have a penalty on the final selling price. You can sell the container with its content at the container warehouse near the old sawmill or put it on the train to be sold via the train trigger. You will be compensated for the shipping container.
Oilseed radish is a special crop, as you do not harvest it. It will be used as fertilizer, a so-called catch crop.
Once the plants are visible, you can use a cultivator and dig the plant into the soil. It is a green manure and increases your yield for your next harvest.

Chaff is made by chopping crops or picking up windrows using a forage harvester and a suitable header. You can cut down corn, wheat, barley, grass, sunflowers, soybeans, oat or canola – even if they aren’t fully grown. Forage harvesters do not have a grain tank; therefore, a trailer needs to be attached or has to be driven next to the forage harvester by another vehicle. Filling silage additive into the forage harvester increases the yield by another 5%.

The resulting silage can be picked up with a front loader equipped with a silage fork or shovel and can be dumped into a mixer wagon, unloaded at a barn with feeding robot or directly into a feeding trough. Silage bales created by wrapping grass bales can be handled like fermented silage.

To turn chaff or grass into silage, you have to dump it into a bunker silo (at the biogas plant or in one of your own silos), compact the heap by repeatedly driving over it with an appropriate vehicle and cover the silo to start the fermenting process. The silo has to be filled at least 10% to close the cover.

For silage production you need to either transport chaff or grass to the biogas plant or ferment it in your own silo. If you do not own a silo yet, you can place different sized ones via the build mode menu. When placing silos, additionally placed silos use a ‘snapping feature’ to fit next to previously placed ones. This ‘snapping’ only works when the silos are empty.
Pigs need corn and sunflowers as feed. More info can be found in the animals section.
Corn and sunflowers are tall growing plants, just like sugar cane. Therefore, you need special equipment.

Corn can be harvested while still growing. This way you produce chaff. Check the section for chaff and silage for more info. If you want to sell corn directly or deliver it to a production plant for further processing, it needs to be mature and reach its final stage of growth.

Both plants need a special type of seeder - a planter - and a new header for your harvester, which makes them easily affordable in contrast to cotton or sugarcane which need more expensive vehicles and tools.
Once the hopper is full, you have to unload the bale. Special equipment is needed to haul it to a selling station or production point to process it any further.
For sowing cotton, you need a planter. Fill it either from a seed pallet or from the silo.
To harvest cotton, you have to use a self-propelled cotton harvester.

In Farming Simulator 25 you can find six different grain crops: - Wheat - Barley - Sorghum - Oat - Canola - Soybeans
They are all harvested with the same harvester and grain header attached. That makes it easier to focus on grains like wheat, barley or oat in the beginning.
All types of grains can be used to feed animals. More info on which grain can be fed to which animal can be found in the animal help section.

When harvesting wheat, barley and oat, you also produce straw for your animals. Straw is the waste product of harvesting and automatically falls to the ground as long as the straw swath on the combine harvester is activated. You need either a baler or forage wagon to collect it.

To gain the full yield, you need to mulch, cultivate, and fertilize between the rows. Special tools are found in the grape/olive technology tab of the shop. Once the grass is growing high, use the mulcher to keep the space between the rows clear. Cultivate after with the Disc-O-Vigne V, and fertilize.

Grape vines and olive groves are planted in rows. Use build mode to place the plants. Place a row by clicking on free space on your land to put down a pole/tree. Then, you just drag the vine/grove across the field and put down another pole/tree to finish the row. Repeat this process to set up your orchards.

Once grown, harvest your olives/grapes with the special New Holland tools, and take them to your production plant, or sell them. Remember to prune the grape vines after the harvest with the leaf cutter to prepare them for the next season, allowing them to grow anew. This step is not required for olives.

Grass, hay and straw can also be pressed into bales. Arrange the swaths first with a windrower for easy pickup. Once pressed into square or round bales, collect them with the bale loading equipment to transport them to your farm or a selling station.

To make grass, hay, or straw collecting easier, it is recommended to arrange it into rows by using a windrower. Grass can be collected with a forage wagon or made into grass bales using a baler. When using silage additive in your forage wagon while collecting grass or in your harvester when cutting, the yield is increased by 5%.

Grass can be cut with a mower, which is usually attached to a tractor. Feed it directly to your animals, sell it at a selling station or let it ferment into silage by putting it into a clamp silo or by wrapping it into a silage bale.

After the grass is cut, use a tedder to turn the cut grass around so it can dry properly into hay. Hay looks slightly brighter and less saturated than cut grass. Hay can be used to feed your animals directly or as part of Total Mixed Ration (TMR). If you do not own any animals, you can sell your hay at a selling station as well.

Despite the fact that poplars are technically trees, Farming Simulator 25 does not require a single woodworking machine apart from the seeder.
Unlike other crops, poplars don’t wither. You have all the time in the world to harvest them. Poplars regrow after harvesting and are used to produce wood chips.

Growing potatoes, sugar beets and red beets requires special sowing machines and harvesters. The easiest and fastest way of harvesting potatoes, sugar beets or red beets is to use a self-propelled harvester. However, a machine like this is quite costly and likely to exceed your budget early on. Remember, you can always lease a vehicle.
A beet harvester can harvest both kinds of beets available in the game. Once sugar beets are ready to be harvested, you first need to remove their haulm. If you are using a tracked harvester, you will need to get an additional haulm cutter. Headers designed for a self-propelled harvester will cut the haulms and harvest in one go.
Red beets do not require a haulm cutter before harvesting.

A cheaper alternative is to use a tractor with several specialized tools. This basically works in two steps: Once the plants are fully grown, you have to cut the foliage with a haulm topper, like the Grimme KS 75-4. Afterwards, the crop can be picked up with a trailed harvester, like the Grimme EVO 290.

The sugarbeet cutter is used to chop sugarbeets. You can find the tool under frontloader tools. The resulting cut sugarbeets can be brought to a biogas plant to be fermented into silage or delivered to the sugar mill production point to produce sugar.
Sugarcane differs from typical field and root crops. It needs more time to mature but it re-grows after harvesting. You need special sowing and harvesting equipment for sugarcane.
Sugarcane grows comparably slow, but harvested sugarcane will grow back after a while and can be harvested again.

To harvest sugarcane, you will need a sugarcane harvester. It removes the top leaves and cuts the thick sugarcane stalks into small, compact pieces. Just like forage harvesters, sugarcane harvesters do not have their own tank, and these need to be accompanied with a tipper/trailer in the field.

To sow sugarcane you will need a billet planter like the Gessner Single Row Billet Planter. As with potatoes, the machines can be filled with sugarcane stalks from the last harvest. You can tip the stalks directly into the billet planter with a tipper/trailer or make use of a telehandler or wheel loader with a shovel attached to fill the machine. You can start to plant sugarcane even without sugarcane stalks. Simply purchase a pallet of sugarcane in the shop and fill the billet planter with it.

As sugarcane regrows, tillage is nearly unnecessary. If you play with 'periodic plowing required', the ground must be aerated after 3 harvests to secure a full yield. The best results are achieved with a subsoiler like the KUHN DC 401, but a plow will be sufficient as well. After loosening the ground, you can plant new stalks of sugarcane.

During harvest, specialized sugarcane tippers/trailers are commonly used as they have a higher tip height, allowing them to tip the sugarcane stalks directly into a truck to guarantee a quick transport. Sugarcane cannot be stored in silos, however, it can be tipped anywhere on the ground and stored there. You can process it further in your sugarmill, which can be placed in build mode.
Rice is one of the new crops in Farming Simulator 25 and comes with new mechanics.

Long grain rice is sown in spring on a rice field that has not yet been flooded. This type of rice has a slightly longer growth phase than the wet planted rice and also produces a lower yield. However, you don't need any special machines to plant and harvest rice, which makes it affordable right from the start of the game.
With this variety, the rice field should only be flooded when the first green sprouts have emerged from the soil, otherwise some plants will not germinate and holes will appear in the field.

When growing rice, it is important to note that the field may only remain flooded for a certain period of time. If the water remains in the field for too long, a number of rice plants will die. Flood the field for about two months before it has to be dry for the third growth stage.
Once the rice is ready to be harvested, you will need a harvester. The rice can then be sold for a profit or stored in a silo.

Rice is sown in spring on the rice field that has already been flooded. This type of rice grows faster than the dry planted rice and also produces a much higher yield. To plant rice, you need a special Iseki seeder.
With this variety, the rice field has to be flooded when you plant the green rice sprouts.

When growing rice, it is important to note that the field may only remain flooded for a certain period of time. If the water remains in the field for too long, a number of rice plants will die. Keep the field flooded after planting for two more months before it has to be dry for the third growth stage.
As soon as the rice can be harvested, you will need the Iseki rice harvester. The rice can then be sold for a profit or stored in a silo.
A mission system which allows you to do farming tasks for the other virtual farmers on your map and earn some money. Please check the contracts page for more info.

On the finance screen, you can see all income and expenditures for the current and the previous four months. The loan you have taken from the bank is also displayed here. If you need more money urgently, you can take loans from the bank in increments of $CURRENCY_SYMBOL5000. However, at the end of each day, you will have to pay any excess interest on the loans you have taken out.

To sell your products, you need to load your products onto a trailer and drive to one of the selling points marked on the map. Open the prices window to see what each station accepts and at what price. Ideally, you want to sell your products at the highest paying station.
Placeable selling points make the most of your produce. Sell your products, either directly from the field or processed in your factories at one of the selling points. Refer to the build mode menu, which products can be sold at which selling point.

You will see all the vehicles you currently own in the garage section. All of your assets are listed here and you can sell them directly from this menu. Their current value depends on their age and usage.
In front of the shop is a marked area where you can park vehicles and tools in order to sell them. Anything you sell this way nets you 20% on top of the selling price compared to selling it from the menu since you went to the trouble of driving the vehicle or tool all the way to the shop.

The prices of all sellable commodities change constantly in accordance with supply and demand. You can influence prices by deciding what you want to put up for sale and how much of it.
If, for example, you only sell wheat for several deliveries, demand will go down considerably and the price will fall accordingly. This also means that prices for commodities you hardly ever sell will go up much faster.

Factories are built to create production chains. Most crops and animal products can be processed into other goods to create additional income. You can either buy the pre-placed factories on your map or buy and place them yourself using the build mode menu.

In Farming Simulator 25, production chains are a new feature that adds more depth to the gameplay and allows you to extend your farm even further, forming an agricultural empire.. You can choose to sell your products directly or continue processing them in factories to gain even more income.

Greenhouses are placeables in the production tab of the build mode menu. They need water to produce lettuce, tomatoes and strawberries. These goods can be sold at different selling points or processed further. You can place a supplementary water tank next to your greenhouse to increase the water capacity.

You can purchase new vehicles and tools from the vehicle shop. Visit the shop directly via the map or press the designated key to open the shop menu at any time. Equipment is divided into categories or brands. If there is a suggested combination for the vehicle or tool, you can select this with a simple button press.
Buying new vehicles and expanding your farm

Over time, your vehicles and tools will deteriorate. Vehicles in need of repair lose speed or engine power.
Take the vehicle to the shop or to your vehicle workshop to pay for repairs. To fix traces of use in the paintwork, repaint your vehicle.
Repair at 100% damage -> 9% of buy price Repair at 50% damage -> 3% of buy price Repair at 25% damage -> 1% of buy price

Certain vehicles can be customized when bought. Each of them has different customization possibilities. To customize them later, bring the vehicle to the marked area in front of the shop, then interact with the shop symbol. Note, that not every vehicle or tool allows for the same level of customization.

In Farming Simulator 25, there are 25 types of crops: Wheat, barley, canola, sorghum, sunflowers, soybeans, corn, oat, oilseed radish, potatoes, sugar beet, poplars, sugarcane, cotton, grapes and olives, red beet, carrots, parsnip, pea, spinach, green bean, grass, rice and long grain rice. There are three mandatory steps to process field crops: Cultivating, sowing and harvesting. Find more info about special crops, and their requirements, in the ‘Special Crops’ section.

Use a cultivator, shallow cultivator, disc harrow, or power harrow to loosen the ground before you start sowing your crops. The implement needs to be lowered to work the soil. They mainly differ in terms of working speed, working width, and tractor power requirement.

Disc Harrows and Power Harrows have lower requirements for tractor power, a lower price and higher working speed compared to regular cultivators. Disc harrows won’t dig up stones. You can also use direct sowing machines. Some of them can cultivate, sow, and even fertilize at the same time.

Regular Cultivators are the most effective against weeds, but dig up small stones. Shallow cultivators have a wider working width and cover more ground while having a lower power requirement compared to regular cultivators. They do not dig up stones, but they’re more expensive and are not as effective against weeds.

When crops are ready to be harvested, use a combine harvester with a suitable header attached. Unfold the harvester and if necessary, the header as well. Turn on the harvester and collect your crop. Unload your harvest into a trailer for transport. It can then be sold at a selling point, stored in your silo for later use or processed at a suitable production point.

- The “Crop types” filter shows on which field which crop grows. The status does not change until a new crop is sown - even after harvest.
- The “Growth filter” shows in which stage the field is. It displays which soil cultivation was applied and in which growth phase the crop on it is.
- The “Soil composition” filter helps you to increase the yield on your fields. It will show, if there are weeds or stones on the field. Remove them to improve your yield.
- The “Hotspots filter” indicates where on the map you can find selling stations and your vehicles and tools. Click on a vehicle icon and the ‘reset’ button to reset it back to the shop. Click on a selling station and you can ‘visit’ it right away.
Farmland view shows you the land available to buy. Click on a field, and it will be highlighted with the price you have to pay in order to take ownership.

The map shows you a lot of information by a set of filters on the left. You can see the state of each field and the growth stage of each crop. With those, you can track which crops are ready to harvest or need care.

Plowing is needed after you harvested root crops, like potatoes, corn, and sugar beet. Plows can also create fields - allowing you to extend a field, combine multiple fields, or create entirely new ones. Using a plow will prevent weeds from growing and increase the yield for the next harvest. Stones will turn up on the fields.

You can also use spaders or subsoilers. Subsoilers move much faster and have lower tractor power requirements. But, they can’t create fields, do not prevent weeds from growing and will dig up even bigger stones.

Another possibility to bring out your seeds is direct seeding. Applying this process saves you one step, cultivating. You can use direct seeding machines to save some time, but always keep in mind that this creates weeds faster than cultivating the ground beforehand.

You can sow crops using a seeder or a planter. Fill the machine with seeds from a pallet or silo first. Select the crop you want to sow. Lower the machine and turn it on. Keep the crop calendar in mind if you are playing with seasonal growth turned on.
Seed pallets can be purchased at the shop. Silos can be placed on your farmland via the build mode menu. Some seeders can cultivate, sow and fertilize the field in one go. Check the shop descriptions of the tools to find out more about their attributes.

It comes with five tabs and several subcategories. You can find farm houses, garages and sheds for your machinery, as well as storage for your crops and resources and tools like a pressure washer.
You can expand your animal empire with new pens here or buy a greenhouse, factories and selling points and place them to your liking.
The build mode menu offers you a ton of options to customize your land and build your dream farm.
But you can buy not only functional things here, but also decorations for your farm. If that’s still not enough, you can shape the terrain of the map with the tools from the landscaping tab.

In Farming Simulator 25 there is a mission system which allows you to do farming tasks for the other virtual farmers on your map and earn some money.
If you go to the contracts screen in the menu, there will be various contracts available, changing over time. You can either use your own machines by accepting right away, or you borrow the items from the employer. You have to pay a small fee when borrowing the machines. The required machines will appear in front of the local shop.
When the work is done, return to the contract menu and collect your money. All borrowed machines will be returned automatically to the owner.
What farmer do I want to be?

Classic agriculture is the heart of Farming Simulator. In New Farmer Mode, you start with some machinery that allows you to start right away. There is a lot of variety in the day-to-day farming activities, with more tasks to do across all the various processes of crop farming.

On some maps, there are readily available animal husbandries on your farm when starting a game in ‘New Farmer’ mode. Animals need food and care to thrive and produce goods but don’t worry - if you pay no attention to them, they will just not produce any more goods.
Wood harvesting is a lucrative profession - although not as diverse as agriculture and operating the machines will require a certain level of skill as well as a good chunk of money.
To begin with, you have to decide what kind of farmer you want to be. There are three types of specializations you can focus on.

If not disabled, the seasonal crop calendar impacts the time frame you are able to plant and harvest your crops. Each crop has its own growth duration and harvest season. All necessary information can be found in the crop calendar page of the menu.
Without the seasonal crop calendar, you can plant and harvest anytime. Nevertheless, the growth duration of each crop remains the same. Keep in mind that prices fluctuate depending on the time of year.
Farming Simulator 25 features seasonal cycles to bring more realism. If you are new to the Farming Simulator series, it can be helpful to disable seasonal growth in your game settings.

You can change the length of a month in the game settings between 1 and 28 days. For inexperienced players, a maximum month length of three days is reasonable. The higher the number of days, the more the game experience lasts and the more tasks you have to find every day to keep yourself busy. A change is not immediate, it will apply when the next season starts.

Snow can be toggled on and off and impacts the handling of your vehicles.
Careful on those slippery roads, better get your winter equipment ready. Be quick and spread some road salt or use a snowplow to clear the roads on your farm.
The game will visually change during gameplay as time passes. The trees sprout leaves before they turn orange in the fall, and in the winter they stand bare without their crowns.

The forecast affects your decisions. As long as it rains, you can harvest your crops, but you have to accept that your resulting volume will be cut in half. Keep an eye on the weather forecast icon in the top right corner. When two weather icons are displayed, the right one will show you what the weather will be like in six hours.

Everything you buy will appear in front of the local shop. You’ll notice two illuminated icons. One for the shop itself and one for the workshop. If you park a machine in the designated area of the dealer’s workshop, you can customize your vehicle, repair or repaint it. It also shows you information about the condition, and value.

The shop offers everything you need for your plans and is divided into different categories on four sets of tabs. The brands tab shows you all the brands available in the game. The vehicles and tools tab consist of various categories. The objects tab offers important items for sowing, fertilizing or feeding animals, such as Big bags, pallets and bales. Note: Most of the vehicles and tools can be customized to your wishes with different configuration and paint options.

The used vehicle sale is the place to visit if you want to save some money. You’ll find a changing set of machinery offered. The discount varies, and can be quite enormous - allowing you to upgrade your fleet sooner rather than later. Mind the fact that used machinery might have to be repaired and cleaned to work as efficiently as if it was brand-new.

Since Farming Simulator offers a completely free game world without any fixed targets, there is not one "right" way, but many possibilities. If you have already chosen which farmer you want to be, start your path. Your goal is to earn money, get larger machines and build a farm you like.
- If you want to do classic farm work, check in the prices menu which crops make you money and when it’s the best time of the year to sell them. - If you want to own animals, find more infos in the help section for animals. - If you want to do forestry, please check the respective section.
You also might want to check the available contracts to learn about basic mechanics and procedures while earning some additional money.

The guided tour at the beginning of each ‘New Farmer Mode’ on Riverbend Springs will teach you the most basic gameplay mechanics and controls for agriculture. This mode also provides you with basic vehicles and tools to start.

If you haven’t started in easy mode, there are a couple of machines you need to acquire to start your agricultural journey.
- You need a tractor, but please mind the fact that every tool has a power requirement (a plow, for example). If your tractor is not strong enough, you’ll have a hard time operating your machinery. - You need a cultivator to prepare the field before sowing. - You need a seeding machine to sow the crops, plus seeds to fill it with. - You need a weeder to get rid of weeds. - You need a fertilizer spreader to fertilize and lime the soil. Not all fertilizer spreaders can be filled with lime, too. Mind the icons when browsing the dealership! - You need a harvester with the appropriate header. Starting with a grain header, since it can harvest a lot of crops, is recommended. If you're playing with seasonal growth enabled, it might be more cost-efficient to lease the harvester for harvest season. - You also need a trailer to transport crops to the selling points.

"Deliver" jobs create a simple task to bring the previously loaded product to an unloading station. A suitable station needs to be selected in the menu. You can also set this job to looping, which means the worker keeps on delivering as long as it is possible. "Load and Deliver" combines several tasks into one. The worker fills the vehicle at a selected loading station, with the requested product. Furthermore you can select the unloading station to which the product needs to be transported. And finally, you can make this a "Looping" job, which means that as long as the selected product is available, the worker will continue doing this task.

There are several different jobs: "GoTo", "Load and Deliver", "Deliver" and "Fieldwork". Certain jobs like "Deliver" as well as "Load and Deliver" can only be selected if the vehicle has a trailer attached or has an internal tank. After having selected the vehicle and the job, you can set the target position. Click on the map to set where the worker is supposed to go and you can then adjust the orientation the vehicle is parked in once it reaches its destination.

After having selected the vehicle and the job, you can set the target position. Press on the map to set where the worker is supposed to go and you can then adjust the orientation the vehicle is parked in once it reaches its destination.

Working a farm can be a busy job. You can hire workers to help you with some of the work. To do this select the map icon in the menu, and navigate to the "Create Job" section. Select an owned vehicle on the map overview to define a job for it. You can also press the corresponding shortcut while driving a vehicle to access directly the "Create Job" section. In the "Active worker" screen, you can create different jobs. To do this, first select one of your vehicle icons on the map, then click on "Create Job". In the menu on the right, you can select what sort of job you want to create.

Working a farm can be a busy job. You can hire workers to help you with some of the work. To do this select the map icon in the menu, and navigate to the "Create Job" section. Select an owned vehicle on the map overview to define a job for it. You can also press the corresponding shortcut while driving a vehicle to access directly the "Create Job" section. In the "Active worker" screen, you can create different jobs. To do this, first select one of your vehicle icons on the map, then click on "Create Job". In the menu on the right, you can select what sort of job you want to create.

"GoTo" jobs are very basic and send the worker to a certain position on the map. "Fieldwork" jobs send a helper to harvest or work a field. Keep in mind that the appropriate tool needs to be attached.

If a certain task cannot be performed, you will be informed about this by an exclamation mark next to the problematic option and a short message. Once everything is set to your liking, press the "Start Job" button. You can see the active workers in a list view with the job and the current activity displayed.

Use the chainsaw of your choice and position yourself in front of the tree. Just turn the saw in the desired direction. When a green glowing ring pops up, you are ready to cut. Just press the respective button. The tree always falls in the direction you are sawing.

How you harvest, depends on the type of tree you planted. If you planted deciduous trees, you need a chainsaw to cut them down. Because of the uneven growth of deciduous trees, it makes more sense, financially, to process this type of tree into wood chips instead of selling them directly.
Conifers, on the other hand, can be cut down either with chainsaws - Cypress and Stone Pine - or a harvesting machine - Spruce and Pine. Because of their long and even trunks, they are perfect to sell or deliver them for further processing.

The harvesting machine saves you a lot of steps harvesting conifers. First, take a seat in the vehicle, select the desired length of harvested trunks with the respective button and drive to the tree. Turn the machine on. Position the header of the crane as far down as possible. Press the respective button to cut down the tree, and it is already done!
You can sell cut trees in the form of logs or wood chips.

You can either sell your wood at the Carpentry, the Sawmill, or the Biomass Heating Plant. Once you have selected the appropriate selling point, transport the filled and secured loader to the respective area to unload the wood. Choose the loader depending on the preferred length of your cut logs or cut them accordingly to your chosen loader - otherwise, transport may be tricky and unsafe. Secure your logs with tension belts. You can do that by pressing the respective button or get out of the vehicle and secure it manually.

Wood chips are shredded wood. First, you need the raw material in the form of felled tree trunks. Since deciduous trees are best suited for processing into wood chips, cut them into smaller pieces first.
Buy a wood chip machine, attach it to a vehicle, unfold it and turn it on. You must now use the crane to pick up the pieces of wood on the ground and lift them onto the conveyor belt. When the wood is properly placed on the conveyor belt, it will be pulled into the machine and turned into chips.
If you have cut logs into smaller pieces, you can also place them on the conveyor belt by hand - but this can take a little longer.
Take a look at the price tab and search for the best selling point. You can either sell your wood chips to the Farmer's Market or the Biomass Heating Plant. Once you have selected the selling point, drive over there and unload the wood chips in the designated area.

Unlike crops, like wheat or potatoes, you don’t have to prepare your soil. You can plant trees on any kind of soil. There is no need for cultivating, plowing or applying fertilizer and pesticides.
For planting trees you need a special tree planter. Purchase a pallet of tree saplings from the shop and load it onto the Damcon PL 75 tree planter.
Position yourself on your property, where you want to plant your trees. Lower the machine, turn it on, and start driving carefully in a (preferably) straight line. The tree planter will automatically plant one sapling after the other. Fill it up again, if all saplings are in the ground and you want to plant even more trees.
The different types of trees vary when it comes to the duration of growth. Depending on the type of tree, growth periods can differ between two and 24 in-game days.

In the building mode, you find a varied selection of trees in the landscaping tab. You can choose from different sizes. The higher the tree, the more you have to pay. You can decorate your farm and properties with those trees - they're not recommended to use for actual forestry.

After chopping down trees, tree stumps are left on the farmland. If you want to plant new trees or use the land for other purposes, you need to get rid of the leftovers first. You need only two things: a tractor and a forestry mulcher.
Position the rear of the tractor behind the mulching tool and press the respective button to mount the machine. Drive to the stump. Lower the mulcher and turn it on. Now, you just drive over the stump. If it is too high, you can adjust the mulcher accordingly. And that's it.

There are twelve types of trees in total in the game, separated in two categories: Deciduous trees and conifer trees.
Conifer: Spruce, Pine, Stone Pine, Cypress Deciduous: Birch, Oak, Willow, Maple, Pagoda Dogwood, Shagbark Hickory, American Elm, Downy Serviceberry
Trees are either harvested with a chainsaw or with a wood harvester machine.
- Deciduous trees are all cut by hand with a chainsaw. - Cypress and Stone Pine (both are conifers) are cut with a chainsaw, too. - Spruce and Pine (conifers) are cut with a harvester.

The thickness and length of the trunk as well as the amount of branches depends on the type of tree. This has a direct influence on the sales value and the kind of processing possible. Trees with a lot of branches gain less yield, unless you cut off the branches. You can use the branches to produce wood chips, if you want to.
Tip: Conifers for timber production, deciduous trees for wood chip production.

You can increase the yield of your harvest by fertilizing and spraying your fields after sowing. Spread fertilizer twice (+23% yield bonus each time) to gain maximum fertilization. You can activate a double application rate for organic fertilizer to reach maximum fertilization, but it will take more time.

You can buy liquid and solid fertilizer in a tank or big bag from the shop, or load it directly from a silo. You can also use manure and slurry from your animals to fertilize, using manure spreaders and slurry tanks. Digestate can be used too - it’s a byproduct produced by delivering silage to the biogas plant.

When cultivating, or plowing, stones can turn up on your field. Depending on the machine type, the size of the stones varies. You can press small stones back into the field by using a roller. Larger stones need to be removed by a stone picker. Otherwise, they will damage your machines. All stones, no matter the size, can be collected with a stone picker, and sold at the debris crusher.

Spread lime every three harvests to gain a 15% bonus on your yield. The field info will show the “needs lime” hint as soon as the field requires liming. You can buy lime as pallets at the shop or in loose form at lime stations.

To spread it on your fields, you need a fertilizer spreader that can be filled with lime. Note, that not all models can be used to spread lime. Look for the lime icon in the shop when choosing your fertilizer spreader.

By applying a layer of biological material on top of the soil, mulching improves your soil, and therefore the yield of your crops.
Use a mulcher on stubble after harvesting crops, before you cultivate the field. This works for any crop that leaves stubble. You will gain a bonus on your yield for the next harvest.

When growing grape vines or olive groves, you cultivate first (unlike with crop stubble), and mulch some time later as soon as new grass has begun to grow. You basically cut back the grass to prevent weed growth. Also, to make everything look nice and clean.
There’s also a forestry mulcher in the forestry equipment category of the shop. This one is used to remove bushes and tree stumps that are left after chopping down trees.

There are three methods to remove weeds: using a weeder, using a hoe, or spraying herbicide with a sprayer. Weeders only remove the smallest weeds, so you need to be quick. With a hoe, you are able to remove small and larger weeds while with a sprayer, even the largest weeds can be removed. But, there might still be some weeds left standing when you only start spraying when the weeds have fully grown. You can buy herbicide as pallets at the shop to fill your sprayer. Sprayers are found in the ‘yield improvements’ category of the shop.

Rolling will grant you an additional yield bonus when rolling over the seedbed after sowing. Small stones left on the field will also be pressed back into the ground.
Rollers in the ‘Grassland care” section of the shop can be used after mowing grass. Rolling over fresh-cut grass will grant you a fertilizing stage for the next harvest. Rolling over grass, that’s already grown, will set it back to the first stage of growth.

Need some new boots or a fresh pair of trousers? Want to change your haircut or want to put on some sunglasses? Not a problem.
Just go to the wardrobe in the shop menu and change your appearance any time you want.
At the start of a new game and during the game you can change the appearance of your character.

With loading machines, you can transport, load and unload goods on your farm and at factories.
- Harvested crops - Bales - Pallets - Manure - Big bags - Logs
All the loading machines help you with a whole set of tasks. Especially when running a greenland operation or tend to animal husbandry. But, some machines are a bit more specialized.
- Front Loaders are all-rounders for loading/unloading. - Wheel Loaders are used for heavy stuff - like logs and containers in forestry - Skid Steer Loaders are agile and perfect if you're loading in narrow spaces - Telehandlers are used if you need to get in high places - like a high-rack storage
For the most common tasks, like picking up bales or loading and unloading big bags and similar goods, a front loader will do the job just fine. But, there's more to it, with basically two kinds of front loaders that are used with tools.

1. Configure your tractor to allow front loader attachments at the dealership 2. Buy and attach a front loader attachment for your tractor in the “tools” category of the shop 3. Buy and attach a front loader tool 4. You're ready to use it!
Using front loader tools with a tractor

First, we have to differ as there are different kinds of front loaders. At first glance, it might be confusing if you're not familiar with them.
- Front Loader (Vehicles) are stand-alone vehicles in the vehicles category - Front Loader (Attachments) - extensions for tractors to use tools, found in the tools-category - Front Loader Tools - attachments for the stand-alone or tractor attachment

You need a tractor, a front loader attacher and a bale spike. If you have only a few bales to transport, you can bring them one by one to the selling station or animal barn. Bale loaders are recommended when you need to transport more bales. Make sure the bale wagon is able to load the bale you want to transport.

Small objects, such as logs and branches, can be picked up by hand and either dropped or thrown. A grabbing hand icon will appear in the middle of your screen, if you focus on an object that can be lifted.

For transporting your logs, you need a tractor and a log loader. As there is no autoload function you have to pick up your logs with the claw of your crane, lift them over the loading area and release them. After that, secure your logs with tension belts. You can do that by pressing the respective button or get out of the vehicle and secure it manually.

You will need a tractor with a front loader attacher and a pallet fork to transport pallets. Use the pallet fork to transport them to the barn and animal product pallets like eggs and wool to your truck or directly to the point of sale. To make transport easier, you may want to own a pickup truck you can load the pallets onto. You can, of course, deliver them with the tractor and pallet fork to the point of sale, too - one pallet at a time.
For more info check “Loading Machines”.

You need a tractor and a trailer to transport and sell the harvested crops. Most of the trailers can transport every loose product. You can check in the shop or your garage, if your trailer is suitable for transporting the wanted product.

The train is available as any other vehicle but you will need to rent it at one of the train stations for an hourly cost. You can use it to load a lot more of your products and move it across the map and sell it. Keep in mind that you cannot transport animals, grapes, olives, grass, chaff, silage, milk, sugarcane, stones, manure or slurry.
Buy or rent a truck with a low loader to easily transport your vehicles and tools to your farm.

The roller coaster is a big project of the town of Silverrun Forest and therefore cannot be purchased. The construction requires prefab walls, metal, floor tiles, long planks, wooden beams, chairs, barrels, buckets, planks, shingles, staircase railings and tables to be finished. Deliver these resources to the roller coaster to start building it. Once the construction is completed, be sure to book a ride!
The southern sawmill cannot be purchased by anyone. You can sell your wood here. To get the finished products, you can purchase them for a small fee.

A second new mission type is the transport mission. You are hired to transport felled trees to the southern sawmill. The pickup points can be anywhere on the map. Be careful not to deliver them to the wrong destination as you are responsible for any damages.

With the introduction of the new vegetable varieties carrots, parsnips and red beet, you now have more options to feed your animals and to liven up the menu of your pigs and horses.
The new types of feed are included in the feeding plan as follows:
Pigs Base food: either Corn or sorghum Grain: either wheat or barley Protein: either soybeans, canola, or sunflowers Root crops: either potatoes, sugar beet, carrots, parsnips, or red beet
Horses Base food: either oat or sorghum Hay Root crops: either carrots, parsnips, or red beet

More pre-placed buildings for your pleasure! This boatyard can be purchased. If there is no owner, it acts as a normal selling station. If you're the owner, be sure to bring your captain's hat. The boatyard requires wood beams, planks, floor tiles, metal, and fabric. Once the boat is finished and launched, the owner of the boatyard gets paid. If another farm owns the boatyard, you can still help by delivering resources, but you need to talk to the boatyard's owner to get paid.

Before sowing the new crop varieties, it is now possible to create ridges with the Grimme GF 800 ridging equipment. This new step not only makes the vegetable field look more realistic, but also adds a fertiliser stage.

The cultivation itself, as with previous root crops, requires specialized seeding and harvesting equipment. With Kverneland's precision planters, the seeds can be planted directly into the ridges. Unlike before, the planting rows can realistically be laid out in straight rows and at 90 angles to each other.

Harvesting is done with a tractor in combination with specialized equipment. A self-propelled harvester is also available. For this a higher budget is necessary, but it has the advantage of higher working width.
After harvesting, the products can either be sold or processed in one of the factories.

There is a new mission type, the deadwood mission. The owner of forest will hire you to cut down dead trees on their land. Once the mission is accepted, an area where you can find the dead trees will be marked on the map. Furthermore the specific trees are marked with an <!> so that you know which are the correct ones. Be careful not to cut down any unmarked trees, otherwise you will be penalized. Once you cut down a mission tree you can sell it to earn some additional money. Make sure to sell all trees before collecting your mission reward, as the forest owner will take care of this otherwise.

Finally there are rock removal missions where it is your task to destroy marked rocks in a specified area. For this you require a hydraulic breaker attachment for a skid steer loader. Watch out to only destroy the marked boulders, as you will receive a penalty otherwise.

There are many ways you can take care of your field to increase its yield: Spread fertilizer twice (+23% each time), spread lime every three harvests (+15%) and using a mulcher on stubble (+5%). And to avoid a 35% yield malus, you have to remove weeds (otherwise -20%) and use a plow after root crops such as corn, potatoes, sugar beets and sugar cane (otherwise -15%).

You can buy liquid and solid fertilizer in a tank or big bag from the shop or load it directly from a silo. Digestate can be produced by delivering silage to the biogas plant. You can also use manure and slurry from your animals.
You can also buy lime and herbicide as pallets at the shop or at different pre-placed silos around the map. Furthermore there are silos that can be placed via the build mode menu.

Using a mulcher on stubble increase your yield by 5%. Another set of tool that helps you improve your yield are rollers. Grass rollers push small stones back into the ground and provide you with one stage of fertilization. Rollers for fields also remove small stones and furthermore increase your yield by 5%.

There are three methods to remove weeds: spraying herbicide, using a weeder or using a hoe. Weeders only remove the smallest weeds, so you need to be quick. With a hoe you are able to remove small and larger weeds while with a sprayer even the largest weeds can be removed. But there might still be some left standing when you only start spraying when the weeds have fully grown.

When cultivating and ploughing your fields, there is always the possibility of stones being dug up. Be careful, when driving over them with your tools and vehicles, as they can get damaged. Smaller stones can be removed with a roller while bigger stones need to be collected. Use a stonepicker to collect the stones on your fields and sell them at the debris crusher.

Hammer time! All over the area, mighty boulders dot the forest. Use the hydraulic breaker to crush the rocks located on your farmland into pebbles. These can be collected and sold at the debris crusher.

Paint the forest! When deciding on which trees to fell and which to preserve, you have a handy tool now. You can mark trees with different colored marking spray. There is also an option for different icons to spray on trees to make sure the correct tree is being cut down.

A new production building! This mineshaft will help you expand your production chain. The mine is working permanently and cannot be purchased. The iron ore is collected in a heap next to it that everyone has access to. The iron ore can be refined further at an iron furnace. This produces metal which can be used in other productions.

You can put your cut trees into the water here to sell them to the old sawmill. If they are shorter than 1.50m, they will be made into wood chips instead. If you own the sawmill, you can also use it as a production point. To sell the old sawmill again, interact with the pond in the build menu.
Throw smaller trees and branches into this machine to produce more wood chips than usual.

The Central European map also has a special selling station to offer: The piano manufacture. When there is no owner, it behaves like a normal selling station. If you are the owner, you can produce prestigious pianos and sell them for a profit. The piano factory needs planks for its production. You can enter the factory and watch the piano being made before your eyes. When it is sold, the piano disappears from the sales room.

In addition to new building models for already existing productions, new factories will also find their way into Farming Simulator to match the new crops. You can either buy the already placed factories, should you play on Zielonka, or buy and build them yourself via the build mode menu.

To get into the rice business, you need rice fields. Like grapes and olives, you can create these via the build mode menu. Unlike with grapes and olives, you do not create rows, but a whole field. Rice fields can also be cultivated like regular fields.
Once the rice field has been created, you can choose between two types of rice (long grain rice and rice). The difference is whether the rice plants are sown before or after flooding. Long grain rice is planted dry and is more affordable as no special machinery needs to be purchased - you only need a rice field, a sowing machine and a combine harvester with a header. For wet-planted rice, you need special rice technology for sowing and harvesting, but this type of rice produces a much higher yield.

Rice fields can only be fertilized as long as they are not yet flooded. This means that you can fertilize the rice field before or after planting, but before the first green shoots appear on the surface.
Weeds only grow in rice fields in the early stages of growth when there is insufficient water in the fields. It is not possible to remove these weeds. In the case of long grain rice, weeds can be removed using the usual methods before the field is flooded.
Depending on the growth stage, your rice field will need to be flooded or left dry. Do not forget to check the water pump on your rice field daily to find out if it needs water or not at this stage. The water pump will only work when necessary.
Besides potatoes and sugar beets, it is possible to grow carrots, parsnip and red beet. Increasing the number of available types of root vegetables in Farming Simulator.

The vegetable family in Farming Simulator is growing. After carrots, parsnips and red beet, you can now also grow spinach, green beans and peas.
Unlike root vegetables, no special sowing machines are required and no ridges need to be built. After preparing the soil, the vegetables are sown using a seeding machine.
When the vegetables are ready for harvesting, you will need special harvesting machines. Each of the three varieties has its own harvesting machine, so you should decide at the beginning which type of vegetable you want to start with, as the acquisition costs can very quickly exceed the capabilities of your farm.

A winch can be used to drag trees from the forest into more accessible terrain. Attach it to your tractor and approach the winch on foot. Pull the winch rope and fasten it to one or more trees. You can control the length of the rope even when not seated in the tractor. There are also vehicles that have an integrated winch.

Hills and valleys make the transportation of logs difficult. A convenient way to transport your logs is the yarder. Attach the tool to an appropriate tractor and find a suitable spot. After that you need to set up the yarder rope by attaching it manually to a fitting tree. Once this is accomplished you can either manually control the carriage or use 'follow mode' to bring the carriage into position. Attach logs to it to transport them over a great distance or through impassable terrain. To attach logs, approach the log and attach it via a rope to the carriage.
To earn money, you need to sell what you produce (crops, animals, and their products).
When it rains or hails you can't harvest crops, you must wait until the weather improves.
Don't know how to do something? Check the Help section in the Pause menu.
You can increase the yield of your harvest by fertilizing and spraying your fields after sowing.
If your animals have water, food, and a clean stable, you can soon expect offspring.
Pigs can eat nearly everything - corn, wheat, barley, canola, sunflowers, soybeans, potatoes, and sugar beet.
Grass is cut with a mower, which is usually attached to a tractor. Afterward, you can use a tedder to turn the cut grass over and dry it to make hay.
Horses need hay, water, and oat to be happy.
Ride your horses to train them. By training them, their value increases.
Using a bale wrapper, you can turn grass bales into silage bales.
To earn money, you need to sell what you produce (crops, wood, animals, and their products).
When you are harvesting your crops while it is raining, your yield is lowered. Best wait until the weather improves.
If a vehicle or tool gets stuck, you can reset it on the map overview screen to the shop parking lot.
Don't know how to do something? Check the Help section in the in-game menu.
Change your environment! You can transform a forest into fields if you want to: cut down the trees, remove the stumps and use a plow to create a field.
Note that you can carry around small pieces of wood by hand if they're not too heavy.
If your front loader is carrying something heavy, you can attach a weight to the back of the tractor to balance it out.
You can increase the yield of your harvest by fertilizing and spraying your fields after seeding.
Pigs can eat nearly everything - corn, wheat, barley, canola, sunflowers, soybeans, potatoes, sorghum and sugar beet.
If your animals have water, food, a clean stable and are old enough, you can soon expect offspring.
Some vehicles allow for additional customization, such as different wheels, a stronger engine, a different color, or a front loader attacher.
Before you can harvest potatoes or sugar beet, you must remove the foliage on top.
You can fertilize a field with manure, slurry, or manufactured fertilizer (liquid or solid).
You can buy new land for growing crops in the map menu. You can also sell land you own if necessary.
You cannot work, mow grass, or cut trees on someone else's land. You need to buy the land.

On the finance screen, you can see all the income and expenditure for the current month and previous four months. If you need more money urgently, you can borrow some from the bank in increments of $CURRENCY_SYMBOL5000.

Selling wood is a profitable business and can be a welcome change from regular fieldwork. You can cut down trees with a chainsaw or a tree harvester. They should be debranched and cut into logs before they're sold.
When selling logs, the length of a piece and its suitability for processing (straight logs are better) determines its value.
Grass is cut with a mower, which is usually attached to a tractor. Afterward, you can use a tedder to turn the cut grass over and dry it to make hay.
To make it easier to collect grass, it's best to arrange it into rows using a windrower. Grass can be collected with a forage wagon or turned into bales with a baler.
Horses need hay, water, and oats to be happy.
Ride your horses to train them. Training them increases their value.

Most of the fields on the map are owned by other farmers controlled by the computer. They take care of their fields but are always in need of assistance and can hire you as a contractor. Check the job board in the Contracts menu.
You can use a plow to create new fields on land you own.
Seeders and planters need seeds. You can buy seed bags from the shop.
When you harvest wheat, barley, or oat, you can create straw swaths with the harvester.
Straw swaths can be packed into bales using a baler. Alternatively, straw can be collected in forage wagons. It can be used as bedding for animals or to make Total Mixed Ration (TMR).

Your cows always produce milk, but you can improve their productivity by feeding them well. The best food you can give your cow is Total Mixed Ration (TMR), which is produced by mixing hay, straw, mineral feed and silage in a mixer wagon.
New trees don't just pop up by themselves. They need to be planted with a special planting machine. The shop can provide you with seedling pallets.
You can also shred logs using a wood chipper to sell them as wood chips.
Bring your vehicle to the shop or to your vehicle workshop for repairs.
If your vehicle is dirty, use a high pressure washer to clean it.

To harvest cotton, you must use a self-propelled cotton harvester. When the harvester tank is full, you must unload the large bale of cotton. You need a special trailer to transport it to the selling station.
